rows.speaker: الشعبي والضحاك والكلبي
rows.claim: They gloss تثبيتا as giving zakat while being content with the act.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي أيضا والضحاك، والكلبي: وتصديقا، أي: يخرجون الزكاة طيبة بها أنفسهم

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وأبو مالك
rows.claim: They understand تثبيتا as confirmation in their religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير، وأبو مالك: تحقيقا في دينهم

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He explains it as sincerity and strengthening themselves in obedience through their spending.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: إخلاصا وتوطيدا لأنفسهم على طاعة الله في نفقاتهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says spenders believe their giving is something for which God will reward them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ومقرين حين ينفقون أنها مما يثيب الله عليها

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: He also glosses تثبيتا as resolve.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي أيضا: عزما

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: He also glosses تثبيتا as insight.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان أيضا: بصيرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: They take تثبيتا to mean that the spenders strengthen themselves; Hasan describes pausing before charity and giving only when it is truly for God.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، والحسن: معناه أنهم يثبتون، أي يضعون صدقاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects an Egyptian proposal that تثبيتا means intransitive تثبتا: an unmentioned verbal noun cannot be assigned another verb's original construction.
rows.anchor: ورد هذا القول بأن ذلك لا يكون بالفعل المتقدم على المصدر نحو الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes intransitive ثبت, meaning to become firm, from causative ثبّت, meaning to make firm or establish.
rows.anchor: إن ثبت فعل لازم معناه: تمكن، ورسخ، وتحقق. وثبت معدى بالتضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the verse as spenders steadying their faith through a difficult act, which humbles the self and makes it yield.
rows.anchor: أنهم يثبتون من أنفسهم على الإيمان بهذا العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the strengthening is attributed to the spenders, min is partitive and governed by the verbal noun; when attributed to the selves, it describes the source of strengthening.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان التثبيت مسندا إليهم كانت: من، في موضع نصب متعلقة بنفس المصدر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari raises the question of what the partitive min means.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: فما معنى التبعيض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says spending for God steadies part of oneself, while giving both wealth and life in God's path steadies all of it.
rows.anchor: ومن بذل ماله وروحه معا فهو الذي ثبتها كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self itself moves and steadies the giver through its faith and expectation of abundant reward.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن نفسه هي التي تثبته وتحمله على الإنفاق في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: He reads حبة with ḥāʾ; the author says بربوة is locative, an adjectival phrase attached to an omitted noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم الجحدري كمثل حبة بالحاء والباء في: بربوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The high ground is singled out for its good trees and abundant fruit.
rows.anchor: وخص الربوة لحسن شجرها وزكاء ثمرها

rows.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
rows.claim: His poem depicts a raised garden between dry heights and thirsty lowlands, watered by itself and bearing fruit at different levels.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشاعر، وهو الخليل بن أحمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains rabwa as elevated land without flowing rivers; the author limits this to the particular garden because it receives rain.
rows.anchor: وتفسير ابن عباس: الربوة، بالمكان المرتفع الذي لا يجري فيه الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden depends on rain rather than running water, as was familiar in Arabia.
rows.anchor: وخصت بأن سقياها الوابل لا الماء الجاري فيها على عادة بلاد العرب

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: He objects that gardens on high ground lack river water and face winds, while hollows collect water; he instead reads rabwa as fertile earth swelling under rain.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالربوة ليس ما ذكروه، وإنما هو كون الأرض طيبة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan had already explained rabwa as level ground that does not rise above the water.
rows.anchor: وما قاله قاله قبله الحسن. الربوة الأرض المستوية التي لا تعلو فوق الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden parable contrasts with the first parable: the stone does not benefit from rain.
rows.anchor: وأنه في مقابلة المثل الأول، والأول لا يؤثر فيه المطر، وهو: الصفوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects al-Tabari's interpretation of رياض الحزن as gardens of elevated ground; it means gardens of Najd, called al-Hazn.
rows.anchor: ولا يراد: برياض الحزن، رياض الربا، كما زعم الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najd's gardens are praised because their vegetation is more fragrant and their air cooler and finer than Tihama's.
rows.anchor: لأن نباته أعطر، ونسيمه أبرد، وأرق. فهي خير من رياض تهامة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: They read rabwa with fatḥa on rāʾ, while the other five canonical readers use ḍamma; the same difference occurs at قد أفلح.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر، وعاصم بفتح الراء، وباقي السبعة بالضم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reads rabwa with kasra on rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: They read برباوة on the pattern of كراهة.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر، وأبو عبد الرحمن: برباوة، على وزن: كراهة

rows.speaker: أبو الأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: He reads برباوة on the pattern of رسالة.
rows.anchor: وأبو الأشهب العقيلي: برباوة، على وزن رسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أصابها وابل is an adjectival clause for garden, following the fixed location description; it may instead be a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: أصابها وابل جملة في موضع الصفة لجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording first gives the lasting feature of being on a high place, then the incidental event of rain; its ordering differs from the stone parable.
rows.anchor: وبدىء بالوصف الثابت، وهو: كونها بربوة، ثم بالوصف العارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آتت means gave, with its recipient omitted; the first object is owner or people and أكل means the edible fruit.
rows.anchor: آتت بمعنى: أعطت، والمفعول الأول محذوف، التقدير: فآتت صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍiʿfayn is a circumstantial accusative, not a second object; taking آتت to mean produced with one object lacks support in Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: ونصب: ضعفين، على الحال، ومن زعم أن: ضعفين، مفعول ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit is attached to the garden by relation, not ownership; al-ḥamza in الأكل marks the thing eaten.
rows.anchor: والأكل بضم الهمزة الشيء المأكول، وأريد هنا الثمر

rows.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read ukul with ḍamma on hamza and sukūn on kāf in the described feminine annexation contexts; Abu Amr also transmits a distinction by annexed noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان، وأبو عمرو بضم الهمزة، وإسكان الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the heavier vocalization for ukul.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالتثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍiʿfayn may mean twice the normal yield because of rain and the high place, twice other land, or fourfold if a double is taken as two times.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضعفي غيرها من الأرضين، وقيل: أربعة أمثالها

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: He says the garden yields three times as much; Taj al-Qurra rejects this as having no basis in Arabic and says the doubled yield is one harvest.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: ثلاثة أمثالها

rows.speaker: عكرمة وعطاء
rows.claim: They interpret doubled fruit as two harvests in one year.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة، وعطاء: معنى ضعفين أنها حملت في السنة مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests ḍiʿfayn can express multiplication rather than exactly twice one yield, meaning many successive multiples, matching the manyfold reward for good deeds.
rows.anchor: بل يكون من التشبيه الذي يقصد به التكثير

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: He supplies an omitted clause after the conditional: if rain does not strike it, as in the poetic example where لم تلدني means she did not happen to bear me.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عيسى: فيه إضمار، التقدير: فإن لم يكن يصيبها وابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, dew substitutes for heavy rain and the fertile land still yields doubled fruit despite less rainfall.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أن الطل يكفيها وينوب مناب الوابل في إخراج الثمرة ضعفين

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Alternatively, dew yields less than heavy rain, but still gives some yield and benefit.
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي: زرع الطل أضعف من زرع المطر وأقل ريعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects proposed fronting and postponement as unnecessary and says the Qur'an should not be assigned a poetic license.
rows.anchor: لا حاجة إليها. والتقديم والتأخير من ضرورات الشعر، فينزه القرآن عن ذلك

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: He identifies the parable's land as Egypt, which thrives without rain and doubles its yield with rain.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم: المضروب به المثل أرض مصر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He compares sincere spenders to the garden, and abundant or modest spending to heavy rain or dew; either is accepted when seeking God's face and exerting one's capacity.
rows.anchor: فكما أن كل واحد من المطرين يضعف أكل الجنة، فكذلك نفقتهم كثيرة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: He compares abundant charity to rain-fed crops and modest charity to dew-fed crops, so a little good should not be abandoned when one cannot give much.
rows.anchor: فلا يدع قليل البر إذا لم يفعل كثيره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He compares the growth of sincere gifts, which God nurtures like young livestock, to vegetation on the fertile raised garden, unlike bare stone.
rows.anchor: شبه نمو نفقات هؤلاء المخلصين الذين يربي الله صدقاتهم

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: He says the sincere believer's expenditure never fails: dew makes the garden good and heavy rain doubles it.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية أن صاحب هذه الجنة لا يخيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses فطل as the conditional answer with an omitted clause, offering several viable ellipses; the simplest remove one part of a clause.
rows.anchor: وقوله: فطل، جواب للشرط، فيحتاج إلى تقدير بحيث تصير جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present verb after fa requires an implicit subject, as in the cited verse, so that analysis also needs an omitted clause.
rows.anchor: متى دخلت الفاء على المضارع فإنما هو على إضمار مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic parallel uses a verbless noun phrase after the condition, like the parsing of فطل.
rows.anchor: ألا إن لا تكن إبل فمعزى

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: He reads بصير with yāʾ, apparently referring to hypocrites, though the author allows a general reference to everyone.
rows.anchor: قرأ الزهري، بالياء، فظاهره أن الضمير يعود على المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read بصير with address to the audience; the shift of address highlights that God knows every deed and intention, promising reward and warning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالتاء، على الخطاب، وفيه التفات

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He takes the final garden parable as another image of the show-off.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي: هذا مثل آخر للمرائي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He reads it as a parable for someone who reminds a recipient of charity.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو مثل للمان في الصدقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والربيع وغيرهم
rows.claim: They apply the parable to someone who falls short in obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع، وغيرهم: للمفرط في الطاعة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He applies it to a person given youth and wealth who fails to act until both are taken away.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: لمن أعطي الشباب والمال، فلم يعمل حتى سلبا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He compares many acts of obedience ending in a final sin to a garden ruined just when its elderly owner most needs it; a similar report is related from Umar.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لمن عمل أنواع الطاعات كجنة فيها من كل الثمرات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says few understand this image: an old, weakened person with many children loses his garden when most dependent on it, just as people most need their deeds after worldly life ends.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هذا مثل قل والله من يعقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza conveys denial and improbability; أحد means any one of you distributively, not an item restricted by a negative construction.
rows.anchor: والمعنى على التبعيد والنفي، أي: ما يود أحد ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He reads جنات in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: جنات، بالجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dates and grapes are singled out as the most honored and useful trees; the Qur'an names date palms while naming grapes by their fruit because every part of the palm is useful.
rows.anchor: لما كان النخيل والأعناب أكرم الشجر وأكثرها منافع، خصا بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He analyzes the clause as a subject and predicate, then discusses competing parses for min.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة مركبة من مبتدأ وخبر

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He treats min in من كل الثمرات as extra, yielding له فيها كل الثمرات, with a generalizing expression rather than literal totality.
rows.anchor: فعلى مذهب الأخفش: من، زائدة، التقدير: له فيها كل الثمرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects extra min under Kufan and standard Basran conditions, and instead allows an omitted noun such as رزق or ثمرات before من كل الثمرات.
rows.anchor: ويتخرج مذهب جمهور البصريين على حذف المبتدأ المحذوف تقديره، له فيها رزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent waw in وأصابه الكبر is circumstantial with an implied qad; alternative analyses take it as present meaning or as coordinated by sense.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الواو للحال، وقد مقدرة أي وقد أصابه الكبر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He allows the past clause because يود can take either أن or لو, letting one construction stand in place of the other.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: يجوز ذلك في: يود، لأنه يتلقى مرة بأن، ومرة بأو

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains the coordination by the sense of wishing: would anyone wish to have a garden and be struck by old age?
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وقيل، يقال: وددت لو كان كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects treating old age itself as something desired; the denial concerns the combination of owning a garden and being struck by old age.
rows.anchor: إصابة الكبر لا يوده أحد، ولا يتمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word أصابه carries a stronger sense of impact than simply saying he grew old, as elsewhere in the garden and stone images.
rows.anchor: وفي لفظ الإصابة معنى التأثير، وهو أبلغ من: وكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kibar means old age; ضعفاء and ضِعاف are plural forms of ضعيف, referring either to small children or needy dependents.
rows.anchor: والكبر الشيخوخة، وعلو السن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine pronoun in فيه agrees with the masculine noun إعصار; نار is the subject of a preceding prepositional phrase or an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: لأن الإعصار مذكر من سائر أسماء الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive فاء suggests the whirlwind strikes after the garden has ripened and become useful; احترقت is the passive-effect counterpart to burning it.
rows.anchor: وفي العطف بالفاء في قوله: فأصابها إعصار، دليل على أنها حين أزهت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire in the whirlwind is the scorching wind; Ibn Masud reports that the jinn-creating samum is one seventieth of the Fire, while another explanation is lightning.
rows.anchor: والنار التي في الإعصار هي السموم التي تكون فيها

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: They understand a whirlwind containing fire as a wind containing cold, biting wind.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، والضحاك. إعصار فيه نار، أي: ريح فيها صر برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parables are explanatory illustrations that make signs leading to truth understandable.
rows.anchor: مثل هذا البيان تصرف الأمثال المقربة الأشياء للذهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection should turn people from transient worldly things toward what remains in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: تعملون أفكاركم فيما يفنى ويضمحل من الدنيا، وفيما هو باق لكم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses transitions from particular to general, allusion, simile, ellipsis, specification, parable, and metaphor.
rows.anchor: من الانتقال من الخصوص إلى العموم، ومن الإشارة، ومن التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb تيمم means to intend or aim; Arabic also has forms with hamza, and al-Khalil distinguishes aiming ahead from aiming from any direction.
rows.anchor: التميم: القصد يقال أم كرد. وأمم كأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabith means bad or inferior and is the active participle of خبث, opposed to good.
rows.anchor: الخبيث: الرديء وهو ضد الطيب اسم فاعل من خبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ighmāḍ means tolerating or accepting less; it is related to lowering or closing the eye and to hidden or sunken things.
rows.anchor: الإغماض: التساهل يقال: أغمض في حقه تساهل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamid means praised, a passive intensive form; its grammatical categories were discussed earlier in the sura.
rows.anchor: الحميد: المحمود فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow is a person's inward commitment to perform an act; the root is tied to fear, and Arabs often vowed what they hoped would happen, including killing enemies.
rows.anchor: وهو عقد الإنسان ضميره على فعل شيء والتزامه. وأصله من الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿma is the fixed verb contrasted with biʾsa; its grammatical rules were discussed at 2:90.
rows.anchor: نعم: أصلها نعم، وهي مقابلة بئس، وأحكامها مذكورة في النحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿaffuf derives from ʿiffa, refraining from seeking something; the cited saying connects restraint from desire with martyrdom.
rows.anchor: التعفف: تفعل من العفة، عف عن الشيء أمسك عنه

rows.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
rows.claim: His verse depicts someone guarding a woman's secrets after nightfall and no longer seeking her after passion.
rows.anchor: وقال رؤبة بن العجاج: فعف عن أسرارها بعد الغسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīmā means a sign; the extended form sīmiyāʾ has hamza for morphological augmentation, not femininity, and the root is related to branding.
rows.anchor: السيما: العلامة، ويمد ويقال: بالسيمياء، كالكيمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥāf is persistent insistence in asking; proposed roots connect it to a covering cloak, covering something, rugged hills, or receiving a share of another's cloak.
rows.anchor: الإلحاف: الإلحاح واللجاج في السؤال

rows.speaker: ابن أحمر
rows.claim: His poem uses ilḥāf for an ostrich covering its eggs with its wings like a cloak.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول ابن أحمر: يظل يحفهن بقفقفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poem uses ilḥāf for people making their robe hems cover the ground.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ثم راحوا عبق المسك بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports give the occasion as people hanging date clusters in the mosque for the poor, then a Companion brought inferior dates believing it acceptable, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: تضافرت النصوص في الحديث على أن سبب نزول هذه الآية

rows.speaker: علي وعبيدة السلماني وابن سيرين
rows.claim: They apply the command to obligatory zakat, permit a small amount as voluntary charity, and take the command as obligatory.
rows.anchor: قال علي، وعبيدة السلماني، وابن سيرين: هي في الزكاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They apply it to voluntary charity; the occasion supports recommending that voluntary gifts be of good quality.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من قول البراء بن عازب، والحسن، وقتادة: أنها في التطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the preceding praise of spending and warning against reminders and ostentation by describing the quality of what is given.
rows.anchor: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها هو أنه لما ذكر فضل النفقة في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpreters take good things as the best quality and khabith as inferior.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على أن: طيبات ما كسبتم هو الجيد المختار

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He interprets the good as lawful and the khabith as unlawful.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: من طيبات، أي: الحلال والخبيث الحرام

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: He identifies the good things as gold and silver.
rows.anchor: وقال علي: هو الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He identifies them as trade assets.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو أموال التجارة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says tayyibat may simply urge spending from one's earnings; the word then describes the goodness of acquired wealth broadly, encompassing quality and lawfulness, supported by Ibn Mughaffal's statement that a believer's property has no khabith.
rows.anchor: قوله من طيبات يحتمل أن لا يقصد به لا الحل ولا الجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What you earn includes anything obtained through one's work, bodily labor, or trade; another view includes inherited property as acquired by the predecessor.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله: ما كسبتم عموم كل ما حصل بكسب من الإنسان المنفق

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: He says earned wealth is singled out because people cling to it more than inherited wealth, so inherited property is implied by the wording.
rows.anchor: تخصيص المكتسب دون الموروث لأن الإنسان بما يكتسبه أضن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive; ma may be a relative pronoun with an omitted antecedent or a verbal noun interpreted as acquired property.
rows.anchor: و: من، للتبعيض، وهي في موضع المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general command covers all good kinds of wealth while leaving required amounts unspecified, so it can support obligations for disputed categories such as trade goods, horses, children's wealth, jewelry, livestock, and debts.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على أن الأمر بالإنفاق عام في جميع أصناف الأموال الطيبة

rows.speaker: خويزمنداذ
rows.claim: He infers that a father may eat from a child's property from a prophetic report calling children part of their parents' good earnings.
rows.anchor: في الآية دليل على جواز أكل الوالد من مال الولد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: She reports the Prophet saying a person's best food is from his earnings and that his child is part of his earnings.
rows.anchor: وروت عائشة عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن أطيب ما أكل الرجل من كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God brings from the earth includes kinds of grains, fruits, minerals, and buried treasure; the wording expresses favor and recalls 2:29.
rows.anchor: يعني من أنواع الحبوب والثمار والمعادن والركاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase omits tayyibat before what comes from the earth, supplied from context; repeating min emphasizes the command or signals another governing verb.
rows.anchor: والمراد: من طيبات ما أخرجنا، فحذف لدلالة ما قبله وما بعده عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem says the initial tāʾ is lightened and discusses what follows when a long vowel precedes it.
rows.anchor: وفي بدئه خفف، وإن كان قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies these tāʾs by the sound immediately before them.
rows.anchor: وهذه التاءات منها ما قبله متحرك، نحو: فتفرق بكم

rows.speaker: البزي
rows.claim: He notes Basran grammarians disallow some cases because they combine two unlicensed adjacent silent consonants.
rows.anchor: إلا أن مثل إن تولوا وإذ تلقونه لا يجوز عند البصريين على حال

rows.speaker: أبو ربيعة عن البزي
rows.claim: He also transmits a light tāʾ reading from al-Bazzi, like the other readers.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي ربيعة، عن البزي: تخفيف التاء كباقي القراء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: He disallows a still tāʾ in forms like يتكلمون because it would require a connecting alif, unavailable for a present verb; connection can make it possible, though Basran grammarians reject some adjacent-sukun cases.
rows.anchor: لا يجيز سيبويه إسكان هذه التاء في يتكلمون ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He insists al-Bazzi's accepted reading is valid by transmission and says grammatical authority is not confined to Basran judgments.
rows.anchor: وقراءة البزي ثابتة تلقتها الأمة بالقبول

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: He reads ولا تأمموا from أممت, meaning to intend.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: ولا تأمموا، من: أممت، أي: قصدت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والزهري ومسلم بن جندب
rows.claim: They read تيمموا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، والزهري، ومسلم بن جندب: تيمموا

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: He also records Abdullah reading ولا تأموا, with the same meaning of intending.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري أن في قراءة عبد الله ولا تأموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyib and khabith are commonly substantives functioning as nouns; explicit descriptions are rarer, as in 24:26 and 7:157, and the prophetic refuge formula.
rows.anchor: والخبيث والطيب صفتان غالبتان لا يذكر معهما الموصوف إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians say the pronoun functions as an accusative object, while the author discusses whether the noun ending is dropped before it.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المعربين: والهاء في موضع نصب: بآخذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse forbids deliberately choosing inferior property for charity; it does not forbid giving inferior goods when they are all one has or are not specially selected.
rows.anchor: أن المنهي عنه هو القصد للرديء من جملة ما في يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa lastum bi-ākhidhīhi may be an independent sentence or a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذه الجملة مستأنفة لا موضع لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: البراء وابن عباس والضحاك وغيرهم
rows.claim: They explain that people would accept inferior goods for debts or rights only by yielding some of what was owed, so they should not give God what they would dislike receiving.
rows.anchor: معناه: ولستم بآخذيه في ديونكم وحقوقكم عند الناس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says people would buy such goods in a market only at a reduced price; a similar report is related from Ali.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: المعنى: ولستم بآخذيه لو وجدتموه في السوق يباع

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: He also explains that people would accept an inferior gift only out of embarrassment toward the giver.
rows.anchor: وقال البراء أيضا: معناه: ولستم بآخذيه لو أهدي لكم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He takes khabith as unlawful property which people would accept only while tolerating its unpleasantness.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: ولستم بآخذي الحرام إلا أن تغمضوا في مكروهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording broadly denies accepting inferior goods by any means, whether as a right or as a gift.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عموم نفي الأخذ بأي طريق أخذ الخبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in بآخذيه is genitive by annexation although it functions semantically as an object; he rejects the claim that the noun's nūn is removed merely because a pronoun follows.
rows.anchor: والهاء في: بآخذيه، عائدة على الخبيث، وهي مجرورة بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For إلا أن تغمضوا, some parse أن as accusative or genitive after an omitted preposition; al-Farraʾ gives a conditional sense, which Abu al-Abbas and others reject because أن is always open and verbal-noun forming.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى معنى الشرط والجزاء، لأن معناه إن أغمضتم أخذتم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: They read تغمضوا from أغمض, with an omitted object such as eyes or insight, though it may be intransitive like أغضى.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تغمضوا، من أغمض، وجعلوه مما حذف مفعوله

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: He transmits a doubled-mīm reading and another variant with a different vowel pattern, both conveying the public reading's sense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري تغمضوا بضم التاء وفتح الغين وكسر الميم مشدودة

rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: The Yezidi form varies the verb vowels and means that one's judgment about it is obscured.
rows.anchor: ورويت عن اليزيدي: تغمضوا، بفتح وضم الميم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He reads the mīm doubled and open.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن: تغمضوا مشددة الميم مفتوحة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He reads the verb with ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on mīm, lightly pronounced, meaning that the giver lets the recipient tolerate it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة تغمضوا، بضم التاء وسكون الغين وفتح الميم، مخففا

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: He explains Qatada's reading as finding people already tolerant of the matter, or entering into it and being drawn toward it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفتح: معناه إلا أن توجدوا قد أغمضتم في الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of charity; the charity's benefit returns to its giver, and God deserves praise in every state.
rows.anchor: أي: غني عن صدقاتكم، وإنما هي أعمالكم ترد عليكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says God draws praise from creation by granting them blessings; another view says He deserves praise for prescribing worship.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: يستحمد إلى خلقه، أي: يعطيهم نعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem shows fahshāʾ can mean obscene speech.
rows.anchor: ولا ينطق الفحشاء من كان منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem says the group avoids obscene speech both among its own people and outsiders.
rows.anchor: إذا جلسوا منا ولا من سوائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If someone refuses to give, Satan may then urge him to answer the petitioner rudely and overwhelm him with insulting words.
rows.anchor: وكأن الشيطان يعد الفقر لمن أراد أن يتصدق، ويأمره، إذ منع، بالرد القبيح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: He reports the Prophet describing satanic promptings as promises of evil and denial of truth, and angelic promptings as promises of truth and affirmation of good; the listener should seek refuge or praise God, and the Prophet recited this verse.
rows.anchor: روى ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه قال: «إن للشيطان لمة من ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise comes before the command because it first makes the listener feel secure with Satan; once fear of poverty takes hold, Satan commands him.
rows.anchor: وتقدم وعد الشيطان على أمره، لأنه بالوعد يحصل الاطمئنان إليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: They take الفاحش as a miser and fahshāʾ as miserliness and withholding charity; al-Zamakhshari sees the second clause as reinforcing the first.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والفاحش عند العرب البخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He disputes that the cited poetry proves الفاحش means miserly: the usages can mean bad character, ugliness, or rude treatment, with stinginess inferred from refusing food.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة في هذا البيت على أنه أراد بالفحاش البخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness as covering sins in return for giving and فضل as an increase beyond the due reward; other views take the increase as replacement wealth or afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: أي سترا لذنوبكم مكافأة للبذل، وفضلا زيادة على مقتضى ثواب البذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promises counter the satanic motive behind giving inferior goods: God promises both covering sins and increased provision or reward in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى في مقابلة وعد الشيطان وعد الله بشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Torah report says God will expand favor for a servant who spends from God's provision; the Qur'an affirms the promise that God replaces what people spend.
rows.anchor: روي أن في التوراة: عبدي، أنفق من رزقي أبسط عليك فضلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāsiʿ means generous in bounty, and ʿalīm means knowing spenders' intentions or where to place His favor.
rows.anchor: أي: واسع بالجود والفضل على من أنفق، عليم بنيات من أنفق

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: He reports the Prophet saying God loves spending and dislikes stinginess, and urges people to eat and feed without hoarding.
rows.anchor: حديث البراء، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله يحب الإنفاق ويبغض الإقتار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also called miserliness an especially bad disease.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وأي داء أردأ من البخل»

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: He reports the Prophet advising people to eat and feed others without hoarding.
rows.anchor: فكل وأطعم ولا تصرر، فيعسر عليك الطلب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: They interpret wisdom as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والحكمة: القرآن، قاله ابن مسعود، ومجاهد، والضحاك، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن طلحة
rows.claim: He explains wisdom as knowing abrogating and abrogated, clear and ambiguous, and what comes first and later in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس فيما رواه عنه علي بن طلحة: معرفة ناسخ القرآن ومنسوخه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح والسدي
rows.claim: They interpret wisdom as prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال، فيما رواه عنه أبو صالح: النبوة، وقاله السدي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم وأبو العالية وقتادة
rows.claim: They say wisdom is understanding the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم، وأبو العالية، وقتادة: الفهم في القرآن

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ليث
rows.claim: He defines wisdom as knowledge and religious understanding.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد فيما رواه عنه ليث: العلم والفقه

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن نجيح
rows.claim: The author counts twenty-nine reported definitions of wisdom.
rows.anchor: فهذه تسع وعشرون مقالة لأهل العلم في تفسير الحكمة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says wisdom is scrupulous piety in God's religion.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الورع في دين الله

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: He defines wisdom as reverent fear.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: الخشية

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They take it as reason applied to God's command.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد، وأبوه زيد بن أسلم: العقل في أمر الله

rows.speaker: شريك
rows.claim: He says wisdom is understanding.
rows.anchor: وقال شريك: الفهم

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He says wisdom requires knowledge and action together; one is not wise without both.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: العلم والعمل، لا يسمى حكيما حتى يجمعهما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He also defines wisdom as writing.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: الكتابة

rows.speaker: ابن المقفع
rows.claim: He defines wisdom as whatever reason judges sound.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المقفع: ما يشهد العقل بصحته

rows.speaker: القشيري عن ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri reports reflection on God and following Him, and also obedience, religious understanding, and practice.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري: وقال فيما روى عنه ابن القاسم: التفكر في أمر الله والاتباع له

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He says wisdom is forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: المغفرة

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: He describes wisdom as an inner light that distinguishes satanic whispering from one's station; a manuscript variant reads inspiration for station.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان: نور يفرق به بين الوسواس والمقام

rows.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
rows.claim: He defines wisdom as having a true insight govern you instead of desire.
rows.anchor: قال القاسم بن محمد: أن يحكم عليك خاطر الحق دون شهوتك

rows.speaker: بندار بن الحسين
rows.claim: He defines wisdom as a quick answer that reaches the right conclusion.
rows.anchor: وقال بندار بن الحسين: سرعة الجواب مع إصابة الصواب

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: He says wisdom is returning to what is right.
rows.anchor: وقال المفضل: الرد إلى الصواب

rows.speaker: الكتاني
rows.claim: He defines wisdom as what brings repose to spirits.
rows.anchor: وقال الكتاني: ما تسكن إليه الأرواح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other definitions include an indication without cause, witnessing God in every state, religious rectitude with worldly reform, esoteric knowledge, and preparing the inner self for inspiration.
rows.anchor: وقيل إشارة بلا علة، وقيل: إشهاد الحق على جميع الأحوال

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says all these accounts except al-Suddi's are closely related: wisdom is precision in word or deed, and Qur'an, Sunna, and each reported sense are parts of that broad category.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقوال كلها، ما عدا قول السدي، قريب بعضها من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom was already explained at 2:129, but further views are given here because they were not listed there.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم تفسير الحكمة في قوله: ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the past form with قد can be the true conditional answer because it carries future meaning.
rows.anchor: الفعل الماضي المصحوب: بقد، الواقع جوابا للشرط في الظاهر قد يكون ماضي اللفظ، مستقبل المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the verb and its meaning are both past, it cannot answer the future condition, so the actual answer is omitted and inferred.
rows.anchor: التقدير: وإن يكذبوك فتسل، فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's paraphrase conveys the meaning but not the syntax: the object is advanced by the conditional verb, not omitted from يؤت.
rows.anchor: فإن أراد تفسير المعنى فهو صحيح، وإن أراد تفسير الإعراب فليس كذلك

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: He reads ومن يؤته الحكمة, with an explicit first object and God as the hidden subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: ومن يؤته الحكمة، بإثبات الضمير الذي هو المفعول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is repeated instead of pronominalized because it begins another clause and to highlight its honor and value.
rows.anchor: وكرر ذكر الحكمة ولم يضمرها لكونها في جملة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past verb with قد is a true conditional answer when its sense is future; when both verb and meaning are past, the true answer is omitted and inferred.
rows.anchor: الفعل الماضي المصحوب: بقد، الواقع جوابا للشرط في الظاهر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reads the indefinite خير كثير as magnification, effectively meaning an especially great good.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وخيرا كثيرا، تنكير تعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He questions an unsupported Arabic construction for magnifying indefinites and argues that the implied أي خير كثير requires evidence; any رجل ordinarily follows the noun directly.
rows.anchor: ويحتاج إلى الدليل على ثبوته وتقديره، أي خير كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic line illustrates deletion of a repeated relative clause when its antecedent is already supplied by من.
rows.anchor: التقدير: ومن يمدحه، فحذفه لدلالة: من، المتقدمة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun in فإن الله يعلمه follows the normal agreement rule for clauses coordinated by أو, which selects one alternative; it may agree with either item.
rows.anchor: إذا كان العطف بأو كان الضمير مفردا، لأن المحكوم عليه هو أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports the rule with examples about rich or poor people, commerce or amusement, and earning sin or wrongdoing; the pronoun need not be forced into plural agreement.
rows.anchor: على المهيع الذي ذكرناه، جاء قوله تعالى: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: He instead supplies a separate predicate for each alternative: God knows a donation and knows a vow.
rows.anchor: حكي عن النحاس أنه قال: التقدير: وما أنفقتم من نفقة فإن الله يعلمها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says the singular pronoun refers to all the previously mentioned items collectively.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ووحد الضمير في يعلمه، وقد ذكر شيئين

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: He approves the collective reference, saying a pronoun can refer to all the mentioned items even when there are many.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي: وهذا حسن، فإن الضمير يراد به جميع المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because أو differs from واو, the author says there is no need for Ibn Atiyya's exceptional explanation; the normal Arabic rule accounts for the singular.
rows.anchor: ولا يحتاج لتأويل ابن عطية لأنه جاء على الحكم المستقر في لسان العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of helpers applies generally to every wrongdoer who cannot find aid against God.
rows.anchor: ظاهره العموم، فكل ظالم لا يجد له من ينصره

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He identifies the wrongdoers as polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هم المشركون

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: He identifies them as spenders who give with reminders, harm, or ostentation, and those who squander in sin.
rows.anchor: هم المنفقون بالمن والأذى والرياء، والمبذرون في المعصية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as people who spend unlawful wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المنفقو الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anṣār is the plural of naṣīr or nāṣir; denying helpers collectively also rules out an individual helper in the context of aid and protection.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم يجد الجمع ولم يغن، فأحرى أن لا يجدي ولا يغني الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from charity and Satan's temptation to God's promises and wisdom, then returns to spending as an act preserved by the One who never forgets; the wisdom discussion is a purposeful digression.
rows.anchor: رجع إلى ذكر النفقة والحث عليها، وأنها موضوعة عند من لا ينسى ولا يسهو

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: After the previous verse, people asked the Prophet whether secret or public charity was better, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: لما نزلت: وما أنفقتم من نفقة الآية قالوا: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: يزيد بن أبي حبيب
rows.claim: He says the verse was revealed about giving charity to Jews and Christians and secretly distributing zakat.
rows.anchor: وقال يزيد بن أبي حبيب: نزلت في الصدقة على اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified term alms appears general, covering both obligatory and voluntary charity.
rows.anchor: والصدقات ظاهر العموم، فيشمل المفروضة والمتطوع بها

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ويزيد بن أبي حبيب
rows.claim: They take the definite article as referring specifically to obligatory charity, since zakat superseded other forms of alms.
rows.anchor: وبه قال الحسن، وقتادة، ويزيد بن أبي حبيب

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين وسفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Most interpreters, including Sufyan al-Thawri, restrict this passage to voluntary charity.
rows.anchor: وعليه جمهور المفسرين، وقاله سفيان الثوري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وآخرون
rows.claim: They prefer openly giving obligatory charity; al-Tabari reports consensus and Qadi Abu Yaʿla chooses this view.
rows.anchor: فذهب ابن عباس وآخرون إلى أن إظهارها أفضل من إخفائها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says concealing voluntary charity is seventy times better, while public obligatory charity is twenty-five times better than concealed obligatory charity.
rows.anchor: صدقات السر في التطوع تفضل علانيتها بسبعين ضعفا

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: He says the numerical report from Ibn Abbas must be based on transmitted authority rather than personal opinion.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا لا يقال بالرأي، وإنما هو توقيف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says concealment is better for both forms of charity.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كلاهما إخفاؤه أفضل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says concealment of zakat was better in the Prophet's time, but publicizing it is better now because people suspect one another.
rows.anchor: كان إخفاء الزكاة على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: He says there is no sound hadith preferring secret charity over public charity or the reverse.
rows.anchor: ليس في تفضيل صدقة السر على العلانية، ولا صدقة العلانية على صدقة السر، حديث صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فنعما هي, niʿma takes a hidden subject explained by an indefinite specification; ما may be a complete noun, or a pronoun referring to charity with or without an omitted annexed noun.
rows.anchor: و: نعم، فعل لا يتصرف، فاحتيج في الجواب إلى الفاء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وورش وحفص
rows.claim: They read فنعما with kasra on both nūn and ʿayn, following the dialect that vocalizes ʿayn; the author rejects deriving it from a form with a silent ʿayn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير، وورش، وحفص: فنعما، بكسر النون والعين

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read فنعما with fatḥa on nūn and kasra on ʿayn, following its basic form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي: فنعما، فيهما بفتح النون وكسر العين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وقالون وأبو بكر
rows.claim: They read with kasra on nūn and a reduced ʿayn vowel; a silent ʿayn is also transmitted, with the first considered more regular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو، وقالون، وأبو بكر: بكسر النون وإخفاء حركة العين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: He prefers the silent ʿayn and says the Prophet used this form in the phrase نعما المال الصالح للرجل الصالح.
rows.anchor: وأما الإسكان فاختاره أبو عبيد

rows.speaker: أبو العباس وأبو إسحاق وأبو علي
rows.claim: They reject the silent ʿayn as impossible or inadequately recorded because it would combine two consonants without a permissible basis.
rows.anchor: وأنكر الإسكان أبو العباس، وأبو إسحاق، وأبو علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects criticism of transmitted readings: canonical readings come by transmission from the Prophet, and the seven readings are mutawatir and cannot contain this error.
rows.anchor: إن أئمة القراءة لم يقرأوا إلا بنقل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وإن تخفوها, the object pronoun refers to the same charity in wording and meaning; treating it as a different voluntary gift departs from the apparent usage.
rows.anchor: الضمير المنصوب في: تخفوها، عائد على الصدقات، لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving charity to the poor calls attention to identifying its proper recipients and confirming their eligibility.
rows.anchor: وتؤتوها الفقراء فيه تنبيه على تطلب مصارفها وتحقق ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ, the pronoun may refer to the understood act of concealment, or خير may mean a kind of good; apparently it is comparative to public giving.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه أفعل التفضيل، والمفضل عليه محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent verse favors hiding charity, obligatory or voluntary, because it avoids ostentation, reminders, and harm; concealing it even from the recipient best protects sincerity.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية: أن إخفاء الصدقات على الإطلاق أفضل

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: A sage advises concealing good one does and publicizing good done to oneself.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء: إذا اصطنعت المعروف فاستره

rows.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
rows.claim: He says complete kindness has three traits: do it promptly, minimize it in one's own eyes, and conceal it.
rows.anchor: وقال العباس بن عبد المطلب: لا يتم المعروف إلا بثلاث خصال

rows.speaker: سهل بن هارون
rows.claim: His poem says God reveals the benefactor's good deeds even when the benefactor hides them.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل بن هارون: يخفي صنائعه والله يظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public and private giving make a verbal antithesis; giving to the poor contrasts in meaning because charity is not given to the rich, implying their right to it and the owner's ability to distribute it directly.
rows.anchor: وفي الإبداء والإخفاء طباق لفظي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: They read ويكفر with the conjunction; other transmitted forms omit it and vary person, vowel, and mood, including al-Aʿmash's yāʾ reading in jussive.
rows.anchor: قرأ بالواو الجمهور في: ويكفر، وبإسقاطها وبالياء والتاء والنون

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: He reads يَكْفِر with yāʾ and indicative ending.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بالياء ورفع الراء

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعمش
rows.claim: Hasan reads yāʾ in the jussive, while a report from al-Aʿmash has yāʾ with the subjunctive ending.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بالياء وجزم الراء، وروي عن الأعمش بالياء ونصب الراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads tāʾ in the jussive; ʿIkrima has the passive form with fatḥa on fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس بالتاء وجزم الراء، وكذلك قرأ عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن هرمز وعكرمة وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: They transmit tāʾ readings with indicative or subjunctive endings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز، فيما حكى عنه المهدوي بالتاء ورفع الراء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر
rows.claim: They read with nūn and indicative ending.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، وأبو بكر: بالنون ورفع الراء

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read with nūn and jussive ending; a report from al-Aʿmash has nūn and subjunctive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع، وحمزة، والكسائي: بالنون والجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers attributing the verb to God, especially with nūn; other possibilities take the subject as the charity's distribution or its concealment, or the charity itself with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: فالأظهر أن الفعل مسند إلى الله تعالى، كقراءة من قرأ: ونكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indicative forms can begin a new clause or coordinate with the clause after fa; the jussive tracks the conditional clause, while subjunctive follows an implied أن, though this source construction is difficult.
rows.anchor: ومن جزم الراء فعلى مراعاة الجملة التي وقعت جزاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He understands the reading as: if you conceal charity it will be better for you, and God will forgive you.
rows.anchor: ومعناه: وإن تخفوها يكن خيرا لكم، وأن نكفر عنكم
